controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py so that solve(data) implements the user contract exactly. Validate that data is a dict with JSON-object 'base' and 'patch', else raise ValueError. Perform a deep merge without mutating inputs: for each patch key, a null value removes the key (no-op if absent); if both base and patch values are dicts, merge recursively; if both are lists, the patch list replaces the base list; if the base key is absent, insert the patch value as-is; if the types differ (object, list, string, boolean, number; bool and number are distinct), raise ValueError. Preserve key order: base keys in original order, then patch-only keys in patch order. Use only standard-library imports if any. The current module.py is a shallow merge and fails the nested-object case, so replace it entirely.

Write test_cases.json: a JSON list of at least four distinct cases. Each case has an 'input' object with 'base' and 'patch', plus exactly one of 'output' (expected JSON result) or 'error' (exception class name, e.g. 'ValueError'). Cover: empty merge; flat add; nested object recursive merge (base {a:{x:1}}, patch {a:{y:2}} gives {a:{x:1,y:2}}); null removes an existing key; null on an absent key is a no-op; list replacement with no concatenation; key order (base order, then patch-only keys in patch order); type mismatch raising ValueError (e.g. string vs number, boolean vs number); and non-object input raising ValueError. Expectations must match the user contract exactly. Do not modify module.py.
